sources.title: The Rigveda: The Earliest Religious Poetry of India
sources.edition: Stephanie W. Jamison and Joel P. Brereton, 2014

claims.subject: vedic_vasisthas
claims.summary: The hymn credits the Vasiṣṭhas’ sacred formulation with bringing Indra’s help to Sudās in the Battle of the Ten Kings.
claims.speaker: Ṛgveda 7.33 hymn voice; speaker division follows Jamison–Brereton’s editorial reading
claims.note: This is a claim within the hymn’s account, not independent historical confirmation. The collective Vasiṣṭhas is retained; it is not collapsed into one individual poet.

claims.subject: vedic_vasisthas
claims.summary: The verse says Indra, acting with the Vasiṣṭhas, smashed Bheda.
claims.speaker: Ṛgveda 7.33 hymn voice; plural referent follows the translation’s ‘with them’
claims.note: The action is attributed to Indra; the Vasiṣṭhas are companions/ritual supporters in the verse. This records the hymn’s presentation, not a verified battle report.

claims.subject: vasistha
claims.locator: Ṛgveda 7.33.1–14; edition heading and translation, pp. 923–924
claims.summary: The hymn moves from Vasiṣṭha and his descendants (verses 1–9) to Vasiṣṭha’s birth narrative (verses 10–14).
claims.speaker: Jamison–Brereton’s edition heading and segmentation
claims.note: This is a same-hymn narrative link, not a claim of biological kinship. The verse segmentation and collective-versus-individual distinction are editorial framing.

search_log.query: Rigveda 7.33 Sudas Bheda Jamison Brereton translation
search_log.result: Opened the primary translation and checked 7.33.3–5 and its introductory segmentation; retained only named persons and distinctions supported by the text.
Cross-checked the Agastya–Vasiṣṭha wording against an online translation with Sanskrit text; used Jamison–Brereton as the claim source.

notes: This sampled addition extends the existing Agastya → Vasiṣṭha witness edge to Sudās and Bheda through the Vasiṣṭha poetic lineage in Ṛgveda 7.33; it does not assert meetings with Agastya.

The Vasiṣṭha birth narrative contains competing and layered motifs. Existing claims about his birth and Agastya bringing him into the clan remain separately qualified; this file adds no parentage claims.
No new claims were added for names already represented in the graph, including Atri, Gotama, Purumīḍha, and Viśpalā.
